content:
I've noticed that Apple seems to have abandoned Cinematic mode, and a video experiment perfectly illustrates my disappointment with this.

It's not that the feature is bad — it's that it's close enough to being good that it baffles me why Apple hasn't taken advantage of the massive performance gains between the original iPhone 13 launch and the latest iPhones. Let me tell you why...

I've said before that I understand why Apple hasn't prioritised updating it, but I also think it should — it would encourage the next generation of video creators and filmmakers, especially teenagers who might not have access to any other camera equipment.

I have a friend who uses a smartphone to approach strangers on the street and get them to open up in ways you wouldn't expect. I decided to flip the script, put him in a chair, and film him with — you guessed it — my iPhone 16 Pro Max.

I wanted to see how Cinematic mode would handle a relatively simple challenge: a person in the foreground, a railing about 25 feet behind them, and then the O2 Arena nearly a thousand feet further back across the River Thames. Plus, he's sitting in a chair, so there's not a lot of movement.

The answer is... close, but no cigar. It looks pretty good overall, but there's noticeable halation between CK's feet and the railing, the O2 Arena's support pillars occasionally come into focus when he turns his head, and the river sometimes snaps into focus when he spreads his arms:

To be fair, CK reckons the average viewer wouldn't notice any of this. If they weren't a filmmaker or a tech enthusiast familiar with how the feature works, they probably wouldn't spot these issues — and if they did, they wouldn't be bothered by them. I suspect he's probably right.

But these issues genuinely bother me, and I think even amateur filmmaking enthusiasts would share my disappointment — and those are exactly the people this feature is supposed to target.

As I said at the start, my disappointment isn't because the feature is bad; it's because I genuinely believe that if Apple properly leveraged the power of its newer iPhone chipsets and neural processing capabilities, this feature could be significantly better. In fact, I'd expect a properly updated Cinematic mode to handle far more complex environments than this one.

Do you agree? Do you want to see Apple pay more attention to Cinematic mode? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
